item.text: The auth server currently stops at the first registered U2F device. Response verification already matches the responding key handle against the user’s devices, so the main change is to issue and carry every challenge. The CLI’s U2F helper already accepts multiple challenges; its login path needs to pass the full list.

func TestU2FSignRequestAllDevices(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	a := newTestAuthServer(t)
	pref, err := services.NewAuthPreference(types.AuthPreferenceSpecV2{
		Type:         teleport.Local,
		SecondFactor: teleport.U2F,
		U2F: &types.U2F{
			AppID:  "teleport",
			Facets: []string{"teleport"},
		},
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, a.SetAuthPreference(pref))

	const username = "multi-u2f-user"
	const password = "password"
	_, _, err = CreateUserAndRole(a, username, []string{"role"})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, a.UpsertPassword(username, []byte(password)))

	totp, err := services.NewTOTPDevice("totp", "JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP", time.Now())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, a.Identity.UpsertMFADevice(ctx, username, totp))

	keys := make(map[string]*mocku2f.Key)
	for _, name := range []string{"first", "second"} {
		key, err := mocku2f.Create()
		require.NoError(t, err)
		dev, err := u2f.NewDevice(name, &u2f.Registration{
			KeyHandle: key.KeyHandle,
			PubKey:    key.PrivateKey.PublicKey,
		}, time.Now())
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, a.Identity.UpsertMFADevice(ctx, username, dev))
		encodedHandle := base64.URLEncoding.WithPadding(base64.NoPadding).EncodeToString(key.KeyHandle)
		keys[encodedHandle] = key
	}

	challenge, err := a.U2FSignRequest(username, []byte(password))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, challenge.Challenges, len(keys))
	require.Equal(t, &challenge.Challenges[0], challenge.AuthenticateChallenge)

	// Every registered U2F device must be able to complete its own challenge.
	for _, request := range challenge.Challenges {
		key := keys[request.KeyHandle]
		require.NotNil(t, key)
		response, err := key.SignResponse(&request)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NoError(t, a.CheckU2FSignResponse(ctx, username, response))
	}

	// The first challenge remains visible to clients that decode only the old
	// top-level JSON fields, while new clients receive the full list.
	data, err := json.Marshal(challenge)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	var legacy u2f.AuthenticateChallenge
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(data, &legacy))
	require.Equal(t, challenge.Challenges[0], legacy)
	var decoded U2FAuthenticateChallenge
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(data, &decoded))
	require.Equal(t, challenge.Challenges, decoded.GetChallenges())

	// A new client can also decode a response from an older auth server.
	legacyData, err := json.Marshal(legacy)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	var fromLegacy U2FAuthenticateChallenge
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(legacyData, &fromLegacy))
	require.Equal(t, []u2f.AuthenticateChallenge{legacy}, fromLegacy.GetChallenges())
}

item.text:
The auth server now issues a challenge for every registered U2F key. [U2FAuthenticateChallenge](/app/lib/auth/auth.go:828) carries the full list while preserving the legacy single-challenge JSON fields. The [CLI login flow](/app/lib/client/weblogin.go:492) accepts either format and can use any registered key. The Go web endpoint exposes the list, and `tsh mfa` is hidden from help.

Three agents handled the server, CLI, and web changes; I reviewed and integrated their patches. Focused auth, web, client, and `tsh` tests passed offline, including a web login using the key outside the legacy challenge. The full auth suite failed an unrelated password timing threshold test, which also failed when rerun alone.

The checked-out prebuilt browser UI still uses the legacy single challenge; its source is outside this repository.
